title: MC-Sparse: Closing the Dense-Sparse Gap in Diffusion Transformers

beats.text: Why do 50% of your GPU cycles waste compute before MC-Sparse fixes the bottleneck?
beats.visual_focus: A flickering video frame glitching into static.

beats.text: The villain is naive sparse attention. It blindly discards tokens, losing critical context and turning high-fidelity video into blurry, incoherent noise.
beats.visual_focus: A library shelf collapsing as books are thrown out.

beats.text: Enter MC-Sparse. It caches metadata of vital interactions, mapping what matters before the heavy lifting begins.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing map overlaying the noisy diffusion latent.

lines: def mc_sparse_attention(q, k, v, cache, step):
groups, kv_idx, residual = profile_dense_interactions(q, k, v)
return fused_sparse_gemm(q, k, v, cache.indices) + cache.residual

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—it immediately called out the inefficiency of diffusion models, which is a pain point I actually care about. I didn't swipe because you didn't start with 'Today we're going to talk about.' Beat 4 was the best part because you actually mentioned GEMM operations, which makes it feel like a real dev video and not some marketing fluff. My only gripe is that 'caching metadata' in Beat 3 is a bit vague—it sounds like you're just saving a list, but I assume you're actually caching attention maps or indices. Be more specific there.
